correctness.rationale: Proof reduces every complex maximizer to a positive two-level vector using entrywise positivity, strict q-power convexity of secant slopes and interior first variations. Polynomial identities give q=2 and q=4. Exact derivative analysis and a one-zero argument for a logarithmic ratio prove that at q*=log4/log(4/3) only t=1/2 and t=1 are global maximizers. Strict log-convexity in q propagates sharpness to all 2<=q<q*, and t=1/2 supplies a strict witness for all q>q*. The ell-infinity limit follows from row Cauchy–Schwarz. The standalone finite checker passed 4,366 assertions and is supplemental, not the continuum proof.

value.rationale: The six-cycle is the smallest connected homogeneous biregular bipartite graph that is not complete bipartite; an entire natural induced-norm exponent line is evaluated up to a sharp one-variable formula and an exact global first-order symmetry-breaking threshold. At q*=log4/log(4/3), two separated optimizer orbits coexist, proving a nonperturbative jump invisible to Hilbert endpoint and standard interpolation. The exact critical coefficient and equality classes provide a motivated benchmark for the emerging graph-shape operator-norm correspondence; this is not a gratuitous single matrix-entry computation.
